author: श्रीमदानन्दतीर्थभगवत्पादाचार्य
commentary: तदेव स्पष्टयति - श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्नेति ॥ पूर्वं श्रुतिभिः= वेदैर्विप्रतिपन्ना= विरुद्धा सती यदा वेदार्थानुकूलेन तत्त्वनिश्चयेन विपरीतवाग्भिरपि निश्चला भवति; ततश्च समाधावचला, ब्रह्मप्रत्यक्षदर्शनेन भेरीताडनादावपि परमानन्दमग्नत्वात्; तदा योगमवाप्स्यसि उपायसिद्धो भवसीत्यर्थः ॥ ५३ ॥
translation:
Acharya Madhva uses this commentary to define what it truly means to be unshakeable (niścalā) and how a perfected soul's concentration is so deep that even a roaring drum cannot break their spiritual bliss. - 

Krishna clarifies and sheds specific light on that very same principle by speaking the verse beginning with “Śruti-vipratipannā” (perplexed by what is heard/revealed). Previously, the intellect was vipratipannā—meaning it was pulled in contradictory directions, confused, or seemingly opposed by the various multi-fruited statements of the Vedas (the ritual sections promising temporary heavens) when that intellect, through a firm, definitive realization of the Absolute Truth (tattva-niścayena) that perfectly aligns with the core meaning of the Vedas, becomes completely immovable and unshakeable (niścalā)—even when faced with misleading, contrary arguments (viparīta-vāgbhiḥ) and consequently, it becomes absolutely unmoving and steady in Samadhi (deep spiritual absorption). Because of the direct, experiential perception of the Supreme Brahman (Brahma-pratyakṣa-darśanena), the soul is so thoroughly submerged in supreme bliss (paramānanda-magnatvāt) that even the thunderous beating of a giant war-drum (bherī-tāḍanāda) right next to them cannot shake them loose at that momentous time, you shall confidently attain Yoga. The deeper meaning is: 'You will become perfectly accomplished and successful in the spiritual method (upāya-siddhaḥ).'
